metadata.title: Data Density Pass 22 -- Day 2 Bigelow's Stand at Trostle Farm (Ticks 296-310)
metadata.description: Detailed regiment/battery records for Bigelow's 9th Massachusetts Battery fighting withdrawal at Trostle Farm, McGilvery forming his Plum Run line, Barksdale's mortal wounding, and the 21st Mississippi overrunning Bigelow's guns. One of the most dramatic small-unit actions of the entire battle.

placements.notes: Bigelow ordered to hold Trostle Farm without support -- buy time for McGilvery to form the Plum Run line
21st Mississippi -- Barksdale's right regiment charging toward Bigelow's guns
Barksdale's 13th Mississippi -- Barksdale on horseback far ahead of his men
Phillips's 5th MA Battery -- McGilvery's line beginning to form on the Plum Run
Bigelow firing canister -- holding the farm lane alone. 4 guns now engaged.
21st Mississippi closing on Bigelow -- they will overrun the guns in 2 more ticks
Barksdale mortally wounded here -- shot from his horse, lying in the field
Bigelow limbering under fire -- withdrawing by prolonge (dragging the guns by rope)
21st Mississippi at the guns -- hand-to-hand at Bigelow's battery
Barksdale's regiment -- Barksdale shot, the regiment loses momentum
Bigelow's GUNS OVERRUN -- 4 guns lost at Trostle Farm. Bigelow wounded. But he bought the 10 minutes McGilvery needed.
21st Mississippi with Bigelow's guns -- but they have no support to exploit
McGilvery's line now formed -- 35 guns on the Plum Run ready to fire
Thomas's Battery C, 4th US -- Plum Run line anchor
Hart's Battery, 15th NY -- Plum Run line
21st Mississippi repulsed by McGilvery's guns firing canister at 200 yards -- Barksdale is dying
Barksdale's brigade broken -- no Confederate infantry can face McGilvery's 35 guns alone
Bigelow's battery reformed behind the Plum Run line -- only 88 men and 2 guns left. They held.
